urls.description: Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) and Congressman Kevin Mullin (CA-15) introduced the Sunlight on SuperPACs Act of 2026. This new legislation will require federal election campaign ads paid for by SuperPACs to disclose the name and dollar amount contributed to that SuperPAC by its top three major donors of $5,000 or more. By providing voters with more information on the funders of election ads, they will be empowered to make more informed decisions about the content of those ads.

We’re continuing to closely monitor the coastal storm impacting New Jersey, with the strongest winds and highest tides expected tonight into Saturday.

Downed trees and power outages are possible across much of the state, with 1–2 inches of rain expected in North Jersey and 2–4 inches along the coast.

Along the coast, multiple rounds of tidal flooding are expected, especially in back bay communities, along with damaging winds, high surf, dangerous rip currents, and beach erosion.

Please stay alert, follow local guidance, and be prepared for changing conditions – and never drive through a flooded road.

Since 2025, more than 20,000 USDA employees have left the agency—making it harder for aid and assistance to get to our farmers.

To make matters worse, the Administration undercut our ranchers by importing billions in foreign beef products. Ohio farmers are already getting squeezed by skyrocketing diesel and fertilizer prices and reckless tariffs driving up equipment costs.

Now, they want to cut $5 Billion from USDA's budget—wiping out programs for new and beginning farmers, conservation, and rural development.

While Washington politicians are making it more expensive to farm, harder to get help, and tougher for family farms to stay in business, I’m fighting to lower costs for our family farmers, expand markets and opportunities, and pass a bipartisan farm bill our NW Ohio farmers can rely on.

text: RT @txcattlefeeders: A joint statement from Texas Cattle Feeders Association, Kansas Livestock Association and Oklahoma Cattlemen’s Associa…

reposted.text:
A joint statement from Texas Cattle Feeders Association, Kansas Livestock Association and Oklahoma Cattlemen’s Association regarding the ongoing ICE operations in Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas:

“The Kansas Livestock Association, Oklahoma Cattlemen’s Association and Texas Cattle Feeders Association are closely monitoring reported U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) activity affecting agricultural communities in Oklahoma, Kansas, and Texas. 
 
Our organizations respect the responsibility of federal agencies to enforce the law. At the same time, cattle producers, feedyards, dairies, livestock markets, processors, and other rural businesses depend on a stable workforce to care for animals, protect food safety, and keep the supply chains operating. Sudden workforce disruptions can create immediate animal-welfare, operational, and economic consequences that extend well beyond an individual business. These ICE operations are having a massive chilling effect on the legal, documented, skilled workers that put beef on the table and keep the cattle supply chain moving. Additionally, these types of disruptions will lead to higher beef prices for consumers. 
 
Reported impacts to our organizations throughout the past few days have been: 
- Thousands of fed cattle slated for shipping to processors now delayed, resulting in millions of dollars in lost revenue and additional costs. 
- Workforce disruptions at numerous supply chain chokepoints such as feedyards, dairies, processors, feed and grain companies, transportation hubs, and community services. 
 
These disruptions come at a time of enhanced focus and pressure on the cattle and beef supply chain. They are a costly and unnecessary impact to cattle producers already suffering from unwelcome political interference to both the markets as well as the physical supply chain. Frustratingly, the harm these actions cause to cattle producers last for days and weeks after such operations conclude. 
 
We urge federal officials to conduct enforcement actions in a lawful, orderly, and transparent manner; respect due process; and communicate clearly with affected employers and communities.”

text:
This week would have been Dr. Jane Wu's 63rd birthday. Instead, her family is grieving after she died by suicide following years of unjust, cruel scrutiny by the Trump administration.

Dr. Wu spent her career pushing the boundaries of neuroscience and building a life in the country she chose to call home. Yet she was treated as a suspect simply because of her ancestry. She was never charged with wrongdoing, and the investigation into her ended without a finding of misconduct. But the damage was already done.

Racial profiling of brilliant scientists destroys lives and careers, drives away talent, and makes our country weaker.

We owe it to Dr. Wu to ensure programs like the China Initiative are never revived and no researcher is ever again treated as a suspect because of where they or their family come from.

This week, I had the honor of leading the Pledge of Allegiance at the Southern New Hampshire Chamber of Commerce Annual Dinner. 🇺🇸

Those 31 words mean the most when they’re freely given, and that’s exactly what this year’s honorees do:

🔑Pat Hargreaves, William A. Brown Businessperson of the Year: Army veteran, Boy Scout leader, and Salem Holiday Parade Chairman. With his amazing wife Lorraine, he built Pat’s Key N’ Lock into a Salem institution. They’ve unlocked far more than doors, from scholarships to Salem’s 9/11 Memorial and Veterans Park. As Pat said, it’s the local shop that sponsors the Little League team. And that matters. 

🎓 JoAnne Desrosiers, Volunteer of the Year: 40 years of can-do service to Salem, helping local students launch their careers.

🌟 Leah Rogers-Curto, Chairman’s Award: a candid leader inspiring the next generation and championing women-owned businesses.

Small businesses are the heart of southern New Hampshire.

Congratulations, and thank you!

BREAKING: Tucker Carlson reveals a jaw-dropping private conversation he had with Trump in which he warned him that the Iran War would destroy America and Trump said: "We all die anyway, so it doesn't matter."

This maniac has the nuclear codes...

"I'm in an unusual position because I talked to Trump," Carlson told Steve Inskeep of the NPR Newsmakers podcast.

The former Fox News host has become one of the President's fiercest critics over the past year, with his most vociferous attacks aimed at the disastrous, pointless war with Iran.

"But you've quoted him as waving off the risk by saying it'll all be fine which could almost—" said Inskeep of Trump's posture towards the conflict.

"You want to know what he said?" replied Carlson. "I'll tell you exactly what he said and I haven't said this but I'm just gonna tell you. And this is a fact. And I could look at my calendar but I had flown back from Tel Aviv from Ben Gurion Airport after seeing the ambassador and two days later I was in the Oval with Trump alone." 

"And he was annoyed that I had given Huckabee a hard time in this whole conversation about Huckabee and I said your U.S. ambassador — and as the son of an ambassador — I know what the job entails," recounted Carlson. "And your ambassador, your representative to this nation just called for rearranging the Middle East and allowing Israel to take parts of Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Syria. Like this is a diplomatic incident and so we had this whole conversation about this."

"But then I said this war is not about Iran's nuclear program, which you told me and the world that you eliminated back in last summer, in June," Carlson continued. "This war is being pushed by Israel with three aims..."

"One, its own regional hegemony. Take Iran off the map. They don't have freedom of movement as long as Iran is a regional power.

"Two, diminishing the power of the GCC, the six Gulf states which are a rival to Israel and are becoming this kind of Switzerland of the Middle East and that's bad for Israeli interests."

"And three, getting the U.S. out of the Middle East because we constrain their ambitions, getting our bases out, destroying our bases. Israel wants our bases out of the Middle East. I said this to Trump to his face in the Oval Office days before the war began," said Carlson. 

"And he looked at me and said 'Yes, you're right. But in the end we all die anyway, so it doesn't matter.' That's exactly what he said 'In the end, we all die anyway,' and I said to him, shocked, 'But what about our kids and our grandkids and like our country and he goes 'Uggggh.'"

"What does that mean?" a perplexed Inskeep asked of the bizarre, dismissive noise.

"I don't know! That's a verbatim exchange," said Carlson. "And you know as God watches I said that.  I thought it was true then and I think it's been proven true now." 

"The goal was to get the U.S. out, to diminish the GCC, and obviously to take Iran off the map and sink it into permanent internal strife into civil war, sectarian strife," said Carlson. "And he said it doesn't matter because in the end we're all dead anyway. And I was shocked by that because it's nihilism and that's the last thing any leader should display or any person should display. It does matter. Who lives or dies does matter. The future does matter."

As horrifying as Trump's anti-human remarks are, they are perfectly in keeping with his personality. This man is an egomaniacal sociopath. He doesn't believe in God, doesn't believe in the rule of law or right and wrong. As far as he's concerned, the world ends when he dies. He couldn't care less what happens to the rest of us.

It's also not the first time that Trump has given the world such an unvarnished look into his nihilistic worldview. In a 2004 interview with Larry King, he shared similar sentiments—

"I try and tell myself it doesn't matter. Nothing matters. If you tell yourself it doesn't matter, like you do shows, you do this, you do that and then you have earthquakes in India where 400,000 people get killed," said Trump. "Honestly, it doesn't matter. That's how I handle stress."

Within this kind of moral framework (or lack thereof) Trump's entire life makes sense. Since he believes in nothing, he has chosen to indulge in every cruelty and evil imaginable. He spent his time on this Earth ripping people off, sexually abusing and raping women, allegedly including children, and then used the powers of the White House to slaughter countless people overseas.

If the Devil exists, this is what he looks like.

Please ❤️ and share to demand that the 25th Amendment be invoked!

text:
Another terrible Supreme Court decision. With less than 40 days until the midterms, the court just let the Trump administration's overhauled SAVE database back into use for checking voter rolls. In June, a federal judge ruled this system unlawful, finding the administration combined private data it knew to be unreliable and that some states had already removed U.S. citizens from their rolls based on bad information.

SAVE was created 40 years ago to check eligibility for public benefits. Repurposing it to screen voters, errors and all, puts eligible citizens at risk of losing their voice. And while states can technically opt out, the administration has reportedly tried to pressure them by tying federal security funding to it.

Federal law bars mass purges this close to an election. The legal fight continues.

I'll keep fighting to make sure every eligible American can cast a ballot and have it counted.

Yesterday, I called for Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell to resign following the release of the independent investigation into his conduct.

The investigation found that he failed to uphold the responsibilities of his office and demonstrated a pattern of behavior that does not meet the standards of this Administration.

He submitted his resignation to me this afternoon, and I accepted it.

Public service is a privilege, and those entrusted with it must be held to the highest standards – regardless of their title.

I’ve taken many oaths over the course of my lifetime of service – in the Navy, as a federal prosecutor, in Congress, and now as Governor. I take those commitments incredibly seriously.

So, here is my oath to you: I will uphold the law. I will lead with integrity. And I will always put your interests first.

As our islands prepare for another storm, Kauaʻi is still recovering from the last one.

Destroyed crops, damaged property, and ponds of dead shrimp have devastated Aloun Farms, Kauaʻi Shrimp, and Lydgate Farms. Kauaʻi Shrimp is now closing its operations, underscoring how devastating these losses are for local agriculture and the families and workers who depend on it.

Seeing the damage firsthand and talking with these farmers and UH CTAHR’s agriculture team made clear that recovery will take more than rebuilding, we need to also strengthen our agricultural resilience so our farmers aren’t left to shoulder catastrophic losses in future storms.

Last week, I met with the International Fresh Produce Association. Georgia is a leading state for watermelon, blueberries, and cucumbers. We rely on specialty crop growers to supply fresh produce for hardworking families. However, USDA has not provided adequate support for our pecan, fruit, and vegetable growers.

Furthermore, due to the tumultuous firings of capable workers in our government agencies, there are not enough staff in place to handle the proper communications or investigations for food safety and nutritional guidance.

As a member of the Food Safety Caucus and top Democrat on the Ag-Rural Development-Food and Drug Administration Appropriations Subcommittee, I will continue to work both within my party and across the aisle to support the specialty crop industry and keep our food production safe.

text:
Today the Supreme Court allowed the use of a revamped Homeland Security database called SAVE to check the citizenship of people on their voter rolls.

A federal judge blocked the expanded database in June, ruling it broke federal privacy laws and warning it could lead to eligible voters being wrongly removed. 

Today's order pauses that ruling while the case continues.

Our Constitution gives states the lead role in running elections, and using SAVE is each state's choice. Federal law also bars most states from systematic purges in the last 90 days before an election.

That leaves the part only you control. 

Election Day is November 3. Confirm your registration is current, make a plan to vote, and help a friend do the same.
#BlueWaveIn39Days

https://t.co/YmC2lrA8ua

text:
Friday in the First

Dr. Kaye Bennett Dotson, a Jamesville resident for more than 20 years, worked as a school librarian, after which she began her teaching career as a Library Science professor at East Carolina University. There, she taught graduate students and conducted research. As a teacher, researcher, and writer, Kaye has contributed to preparing the future generation of librarians to help others.

Having retired from East Carolina University, Kaye moved back to her native town where she helped set up a community lending library in The Friendly Spot, which also includes a community café, a food pantry, and a community garden.

We pay tribute to the achievements of Dr. Kaye Bennett Dotson, who has brought her devotion to education back to her hometown and created a wonderful place for learning and community.

#FridaySpotlight

text:
The threat of a Nor’easter could not stop crabs, clams and company on the Eastern Shore!

It was great to be back in Crisfield for the 49th J. Millard Tawes Crab and Clam Bake – a true celebration of Maryland’s bay heritage, watermen, and seafood. Even with the crazy wind, I appreciated the chance to talk with locals about the threats of flooding and the work we’re doing in Congress to ensure our Bay communities can continue to live, work, and play on the Chesapeake for generations to come.

Thank you to Crisfield Mayor Darlene Taylor and the Crisfield Chamber of Commerce for hosting this can’t miss, Maryland tradition!
